key_insight: FracGen learns fracture-aware video generation from a single intact image by jointly predicting physical state maps and RGB frames, enabling controllable, material-specific tearing dynamics.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical way to synthesize physically plausible fracture scenarios for solid mechanics analysis, dataset augmentation, and visual design without running expensive scene-specific simulation at test time.
method: Builds FracSim, a fracture-aware MPM simulation pipeline with a continuum damage model to generate paired fracture videos and dense pixel-aligned physical fields.
Trains FracGen to predict physical maps alongside video, so the model learns internal state rather than only appearance.
Uses physics-informed losses to enforce consistency across predicted fracture fields and improve physical plausibility.
evidence_signal: The paper introduces a new benchmark for physical plausibility and reports that FracGen outperforms prior video generation baselines in both physical and visual fidelity.
watch_item: Performance and realism may depend on the quality and coverage of the simulated training data, and generalization to unseen materials or fracture regimes may still require care.
paper_title: FracGen: Learning How Objects Stretch and Tear with Physics-Informed Video Generation
